jobs.description_excerpt: The University of Nevada, Reno (UNR) appreciates your interest in employment at our growing institution. We want your application process to go smoothly and quickly. Job Description The School of Mechanical, Industrial and Materials Engineering at the University of Nevada, Reno, is seeking a full-time Postdoctoral Researcher to work at the intersection of machine learning, manufacturing, and engineering design under the supervision of Professor Sara Shonkwiler. The position will focus on developing data-driven methods to help engineers improve part design, manufacturability, and mechanical performance. Our research asks a broad question: How can we effectively leverage the growing amount of engineering data to improve the design and manufacturing of mechanical systems? The lab's overarching goal is to improve the manufacturing product-development cycle by developing data-driven tools that assist engineers while rigorously evaluating when and how machine learning provides meaningful advantages over conventional engineering approaches. The Postdoctoral Researcher will work closely with Dr. Shonkwiler and have opportunities to lead research projects, develop new research ideas, publish scholarly work, contribute to grant proposals, collaborate with academic and industry partners, and mentor graduate and undergraduate students. This is a full-time, one-year appointment, with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance and the availability of funding. The anticipated start date is 01/01/2027 or as soon as possible. Potential Research Areas The postdoctoral researcher will have flexibility to shape their research within the broader goals of the lab. Potential projects include: Machine learning for CAD and 3D geometry , including investigating how representations such as voxel grids, meshes, point clouds, and other geometric representations affect model performance and data efficiency. Data-driven manufacturability and part-quality prediction , particularly for metal additive manufacturing and other advanced manufacturing processes. Machine-learning surrogate models for engineering simulation , including predicting stress, distortion, or other mechanical responses traditionally evaluated using computationally expensive FEA. Generative AI for engineering design and CAD , including methods for generating engineering geometries that satisfy manufacturing and performance constraints. Closed-loop design and analysis , where generated or modified CAD models are automatically evaluated using data-driven engineering models and iteratively improved. This design-generation → engineering-analysis → redesign loop is a major long-term research direction for the lab. Engineering machine-learning datasets and benchmarking , including understanding the effects of dataset size, geometric representation, model architecture, and training methodology on predictive performance. The lab's existing work includes a database of more than 500,000 real-world mechanical parts represented in multiple geometric formats. The exact research direction can be tailored to the postdoctoral researcher's background and interests. Required Qualifications Ph.D. in mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, industrial engineering, computer science, or a closely related field. Completion of a doctoral degree in the appropriate discipline is required. The doctoral degree must have been completed within the five years immediately preceding the first date of appointment as a postdoctoral fellow at the University. The individual cannot have held previous positions in the professional ranks. Preferred Qualifications Strong candidates will have experience in one or more of the following areas: Data-driven manufacturing research Machine learning/deep learning 3D machine learning, including voxel-, mesh-, or point-cloud-based methods CAD and computational geometry Finite element analysis/computational mechanics Additive manufacturing Generative AI or generative design Scientific computing and Python/PyTorch Candidates do not need experience in all of these areas. Applicants with strong expertise in either machine learning/computational methods or manufacturing/mechanical engineering who are interested in expanding into the other area are encouraged to apply. Compensation Grade Postdoctoral Scholar To view the salary schedule for this position, please visit: Salary Schedules . Salary is competitive and commensurate with related education and experience. Pennington Engineering Building houses an ISO-5 (CLASS 100) cleanroom. School resources include access to the University’s High Performance Computing facility and secured space for the new aerospace and industrial engineering programs. In addition, the school is developing new Industrial Engineering facilities to support a Smart Factory/Flexible Manufacturing System learning environment, including space for industrial automation equipment, student work areas, vision systems, and related manufacturing and logistics training platforms. About the College Join the College of Engineering at the University of Nevada, Reno. We value faculty and staff as partners in our mission to deliver outstanding education, research and engagement. Our college seeks individuals committed to: Engaging in impactful outreach Providing state-of-the-art education Fostering respect, inclusiveness and diversity Nevada Engineering is a fast-growing college, with research expenditure that has doubled over the past nine years. Supported by an Engineering Research Office, the college recorded $24 million in expenditures in FY26 and offers professional development resources to ensure success. We offer bachelor’s, graduate degrees and certificates through three schools: Civil, Chemical and Environmental Engineering Computer Science, Electrical, and Biomedical Engineering Mechanical, Industrial, and Materials Engineering Our specialized facilities include the Center for Civil Engineering Earthquake Research, Cybersecurity Center, the Nanofabrication Lab in the Davidson Foundation Cleanroom and the Nevada Water Innovation Institute. Located near the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center and offering ready access to the bustling California economy, Nevada Engineering collaborates with leading tech firms and advance research in robotics, AI, battery technology, aerospace, water systems and sustainable energy. jobs.description_excerpt:
LISC is one of the country’s largest community development organizations, helping forge vibrant, resilient communities across America. LISC works with residents and partners to close gaps in health, wealth, and opportunity so that people and places can thrive. We do this by acting as a conduit for grants, loans and equity--and by providing technical assistance and capacity building--to locally rooted organizations that carry out the work in communities.

Position Description:

The LISC National Housing Strategy supports the OneLISC platform by leveraging LISC’s four affiliates to expand housing production nationwide. Through innovative financing structures, impactful program initiatives, and a strong national messaging campaign, LISC positions itself as a leading voice and thought leader in the U.S. housing sector. The LISC National Housing Strategic Initiatives Team seeks a professional to fill the full-time position of Senior Program Officer to provide technical assistance and capacity building support to local offices across the LISC network to replicate and scale housing programs. The Senior Program Officer, National Housing will vet and evaluate opportunities as we look to expand programs and investment in non-LISC markets through research, data analytics, and conducting market studies. The position collaborates with LISC local offices, national partners, community-based organizations, financial institutions, government agencies, and philanthropic funders to develop scalable housing solutions that respond to local needs while advancing national organizational priorities. The position also reinforces LISC's core values by promoting collaboration across departments, accountability for program results, respect for community partners, and belonging through inclusive engagement and capacity-building practices. The position will report to the Senior Director of National Housing and works closely with other team members.

For more information visit https://www.lisc.org/our-initiatives/affordable-housing/our-strategy/.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the planning, development, implementation, and evaluation of national housing initiatives.
  • Translate LISC's national housing priorities into actionable programs, work plans, and measurable outcomes.
  • Identify opportunities to replicate and scale successful housing models across LISC markets.
  • Develop strategies that address affordable housing production, housing preservation, and access to homeownership.

Specifically, the Senior Program Officer will be responsible for the following:

  • Providing leadership and technical assistance across our four program pillars:
    • Home Repair Supports
    • Faith-Based and Mission-Driven Development
    • Developer Training and Capacity Building
    • Homeownership Access and Readiness
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with philanthropic organizations, government agencies, CDFIs and other housing stakeholders.
  • Prepare funding proposals, grant applications, program budgets, and funder reporting.
  • Draft communication pieces including white papers, blog posts, and op-eds.
  • Develop program metrics and work closely with local offices and partners to track those metrics.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage public and private investment to expand housing impact.
  • Travel frequently as this position is fully remote; represent LISC in national convenings, panels/workshops, working groups and other collaborative events.
  • Ensure data, community input and local office priorities inform program design and implementation.
  • Manage program budgets, grant deliverables, consultant agreements, and expenditures.
  • Support compliance with contractual requirements, reporting obligations, and LISC financial policies and procedures.
  • Utilize technology and data management platforms to streamline operations and strength accountability.
  • Develop and implement systems for program tracking, performance measurement, and reporting.
  • Analyze data into actionable recommendations for scaling programs.
  • Facilitate peer learning, communities of practice, and knowledge sharing across LISC markets.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university required. Master’s degree in urban planning, public administration, community development, or related field preferred.
  • Minimum 6 years’ relevant work experience in developing and leading programs focused on community development or related fields.
  • Knowledge of affordable housing finance, housing preservation, homeownership programs, and community development strategies.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple, complex work streams at various stages and coordinate with multiple internal and external parties to meet established deadlines.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with colleagues and representatives from the nonprofit, corporate, philanthropic and public sectors, and demonstrate flexibility and poise in dealing with a diverse range of individuals and organizations.
  • Entrepreneurial spirit and ability to work independently on multiple tasks and projects, set priorities for a challenging workload, and be a positive, solution-oriented professional.
